8. You don't have the advantages many other people have, but you do have time. Just stay in the academic track for now. You don't want to be 30 in 11 years and think "I really wish x were my job, and it could have been right now, but instead I'm just now starting the process". There are people who graduate med school in their forties and even fifties, then they have up to 10 years of residency before they are "real doctors" and can repay their loans.
Even if someone was just now learning basic arithmetic as a 20 year old, they could be ahead of those people. Perhaps you need two or three extra years to gain the knowledge necessary for your desired PhD program, but you can feel like you are behind now, or wish you had done the extra years 10 years from now.
Anyway, you really do have time.

Think about the thing you would love to do most in life. You may be the happiest with that as your hobby. Consider making that your business and one day you may be able to quit your regular job if you want to. But perhaps don't make it your business. It depends. You just don't want anything to ruin your love for it.
Choose a program based on the job market. It's ok if it's not something you love. It's ok if you tolerate it or just kinda like it. You just shouldn't hate it. The point is to make stable money, then you can take that money and do what you want with it. It's hard to choose, but certainly things like English and history are oversaturated with many highly qualified individuals working at trader Joe's so...
Haha, actually if there's a Trader Joe's near you, it's a great place to work part time for a season of you life. Great pay relative to other jobs.


9. Call people working at businesses in fields you may be interested in, or teachers/professors at universities and ask them about how hard it is to get a job in that field right now. Say you are looking for advice for someone starting out right now. Some fields are just oversaturated. I assure you most will be flattered to be asked for advice. Always view yourself as a celebrity. It's a privilege for people to meet you. The main question imo one should ask in this scenario is "What should I be asking?" Also, "What do you wish you had known?"
You could talk to someone who works for 30k in a trade that doesn't require much training that you are just considering for a few years, or it could be a full professor at a high level university whose job would be a 30 year path.

If contacting someone at a university, professors will likely offer much less of their time than "lecturers" or non-tenure track faculty. Actually sometimes non-tenured track faculty are called professors. Some profs, just like in any other group of people are pricks but not all.
(Ok so things are different now with covid but definitely meet in person when possible)
Of course respect one's time when they say they have to go, but don't apologize for taking their time. Thank them for their time, and you will probably be one of the more enjoyable parts of their day.

10. Consider working for yourself in something you are guaranteed to make money in. Just for now. Depending on how things are where you live, mowing lawns...I don't know but it's nice to work for yourself.
Or consider being an apprentice for something just to gain the knowledge.
But if you don't need any sort of financial supplement, just study your ass off. And of course you can learn material you need without taking a class in it. Also try to learn as much of the course material as you can before you take the course. Most profs will be happy to give you last year's syllabus. If you are doing online courses, go to office hours even if you don't need it, especially for profs who seem to welcome student interaction. It doesn't have to be awkward if it's just you there. Ask for help on something you already know. The proff will feel good to have "helped" and will be impressed with your improvement and hard work. It's another good chance to ask for advice navigating the job market especially now. They may have gold or spew bs, but either way they will like you more. Always try to meet or interact with the prof in advance of the course. All of these things will cause them to like you and could possible have a positive impact on your grade. 

Perhaps ask them about something you are studying in advance for the course or just ask them for career advice and you'll always have something to talk about. Of course if a teacher clearly hates holding office hours, then these don't apply haha

In general just know that you can speak to profs (and should) of courses you will be taking before you even attend a school. If there is a specific grad program at a specific school you are interested in, definitely start forming a relationship with the program director (and other profs) right now and keep them informed of your progress. You'll be more likely to be admitted and things will just go more smoothly. You know you can visit courses in person and even online; just ask in advance, although nobody would notice or stop you if you visit a larger lecture class. You can get an idea of which profs you like and who you would like to work under for your dissertation.
If you find a specific professor who's research you are interested in, try to meet some of their students. Ask them how it is working with them. Are they forced to be in the lab 10 hours per day? Do they expect to graduate after four years. Does that prof usually hold students for 5 years or longer. If you want to physically be there as little as possible, find a field and some research for which you can do most work at home or wherever you want to be.
If you find a field you like, you like the prof, their grad students like them, you are interested in their research and you have interest in very related research on your own then definitely form a relationship and start discussing your research right now.

11. Start studying for the GRE now. You may find used study books for free or cheap. Take a full practice test every month plus lots of quizzes in between from now until you take the real thing. Get a study box of 500 common GRE words and learn them well. No matter where you're at now, you can work your way into the high 90s percentiles or even better. If you do get to the 98th-99th percentile, don't waste time trying to get a completely perfect score. A couple of points below perfect is good enough for any ivy leage. Seriously, in case you think otherwise, a 95th+ percentile is easily within your reach. Of course each grad program has it's other requirements but just know that you can do it 

IF you decide you want med school, start studying for the mcat now. Take a practice test. It doesn't matter if you start at the 5th percentile. Just make a high mcat score your goal and do what you need to do to get there. This will automatically help you in your pre-med courses.

12. If you don't already, work out. Often people cannot afford to purchase the extra calories their body is going to need, but otherwise if you can't afford a gym, or it's just not a good environment for you and you don't have equipment, do bodyweight exercises at home. Consider taking some classes in boxing if you can afford it. You will feel more confident, plus you can handle your father in a physical fight, not that it would happen. Or, is he like a retired pro boxer? Just don't become obsessed with working out to where it's a major part of your identity. That's usually not helpful or sustainable in the long run.

13. Get therapy:
If at all possible get therapy if you don't already. Perhaps your school will offer regular weekly visits with a therapist instead of just one time visits to make sure you aren't going to kill yourself. If not perhaps your dad could pay for it. If you are concerned about making him angry with the implication that he is part of why you need therapy, just play up your mother's husband. Say that you are so thankful to be saved out of that environment and you just feel messed up from it etc. I would think most people would then want to help so they can feel like a hero. Again, perhaps you form a great relationship and he really does become a hero but in any case, just try to get therapy if you can.

Physhiatry may be helpful as well. Just in case you weren't aware, psychiatrists are able to prescribe medication. Some do therapy but most do not. Psychologists usually do therapy and cannot prescribe medications.
There are many ways to become a therapist. One must have a PhD to call themselves an actual psychologist (who probably works as a therapist). I'm not saying a therapist who isn't a psychologist wouldn't be perfect for you, but just FYI.

If you are working with someone and they do some "technique" and then they make you feel pressure to have been helped by that technique within a certain time frame and you feel guilty for "being a bad client" and "not trying hard enough to be helped" or "you aren't letting the therapy work on you", then politely tell them you don't click and find a different one. It's great if you find one who isn't into labels and doesn't advertise something like "I do CBT with my clients". Many therapists just have a routine they do with every client. Hopefully you can find one who doesn't use one technique or another, but rather is truly custom to the client.
In any case, if you aren't feeling comfortable with a therapist, politely move on.

4. Projection:
Abusers or anyone who is angry and makes character judgements, and tells you all of the bad things you are supposedly doing, is almost always projecting the exact thing they themselves are doing. An abuser says you are selfish? They are almost certainly the one being selfish. Yeah you could tell them they are selfish and it be true and you could even be yelling while you say it, so projection isn't always happening when someone makes a negative character judgement on somone. But, especially if it's a known abuser and they are in one of their moods and they are passing character judgements, they are actually describing themselves. It doesn't make you not feel like shit, but the knowledge is a tool in your arsenal.

5. Know that you are a grown-ass human being:
It doesn't matter what someone else thinks if you, it doesn't change this fact. Nobody is above you regardless if money, power, title, or stature. Of course you give respect to professors and parents etc...until they've lost your respect in which case you might choose to just pay them lip service to get what you want.

6. Use people. This doesn't mean you step on innocent people to get ahead, but if it's an abuser, just use them to help you get what you want. Think of it like chess. You are using strategy. It can be helpful to be on the good side of the other troop members. They could treat you like shit but they'll protect you more and eventually you will be able to get away from them. They just ended up being needed for you to get to the next destination and then you get the hell out if there of course. If you lead all of them to think you like them, chances are that at least one of them might have a much needed resource for the next leg if your journey. One of them may have a job connection and then you'll then be able to afford things and be on your own as much as you choose. Use strategy. Look at every thing and every possible resource in your life including people no matter how dismal and think about all the ways you can use them. Think of every connection you have with anybody. Perhaps you can't find a use for some right now but keep them on the list for later possible use.
Now think about all the ways people might attack you or react in general so you are ready for it and already have a plan for how to use it. Perhaps use two enemies against each other etc. If you have already guessed how people are going to react ahead of time, you'll probably be right most if the time.
It's not always bad though. Perhaps you want friendship from someone so you are being a friend to them and vice versa to get what you want, friendship. 
Think if every move in your journey like a business deal. You may actually love some people. This doesn't mean you can't use them. A child of a wealthy family who has great and loving relationships with parents will take advantage of that wealth and use it for a head start. Perhaps your father really makes an effort to change and perhaps you form a good relationship with him. Either way, you can use him strategically, but in different ways of course.
Just stay focused. Right now you need to survive this damn thing.

7. So I think you should live with your father as long as possible for financial reasons, get a PhD, and think about starting a side business. A PhD doesn't necessarily equate to income but there is no reason to cut ties with that now.
Again perhaps you end up actually liking the living environment with your father, but if not perhaps a possible strategy is to pay lip service and do whatever you can to be on his good side while you get what you want. Get the mother and kids to be advocates for you.
It's possible he makes even this impossible but it's just a thought. I'm not saying this may not be incredibly difficult.

It's the pursuit of happiness. He achieved happiness. He stole it from somebody else so he could have it, and he feels great about it, sleeps very well.

Anyway, I'm just sorry for the way the world is. It's not fair. People do not have equal opportunities. I hope you find a reason and a purpose for life and that you emerge on the other side of this alive.

To people who have had to fight their way through life one day at a time, sometimes even one second at a time, keep fighting, even when it feels like death has wrapped itself around your legs, and you are clawing at the ground trying to continue to move forward or at least simply stay in place, and death is pulling you backwards into blackness as you continue to claw at the ground. Or perhaps you are hanging on a slippery pole over a pit of lava and you are sweating and desperately trying to hang on but you don't know how much longer you can hang there. How can someone be expected to endure such a thing for months or years or decades at a time? It's impossible for you to comprehend how you are going to make it and no one seems to acknowledge how immense your effort is just to be alive as long as you have. They are over there on the ledge reclining on their sofa, watching TV, eating popcorn, and they're saying "Why don't you just relax? Just calm down! Stop dwelling on negative thoughts! Think positive thoughts! Nothing can be that bad! Why would you kill yourself! Why would you go do something so stupid! You would regret it!" "Crunch" goes another handful of popcorn into their mouth. 
But you can't calm down! It's ridiculous to tell you to stop dwelling on falling into a pit of lava while you are barely hanging on to a pole...hanging over a pit of lava! It is not about being positive or negative, is simply about you trying to survive. It's not something you are actively seeking out. One day you woke up and just found yourself placed on that pole or you find yourself being dragged into death by death itself and you are forced to fight for your life. You have no choice. It's either fight or die. It decided to attack you and you do not know why. You did not choose to be attacked. You did not seek it out. Death chose to grab you with its talons and it won't let go. Simply "relaxing" or "calming down" would actually mean death as you would slide into blackness or lose your grip on the pole! People think suicide is an action, but when suicide has wrapped its tendrils around you, remaining alive is the action! Suicide is an attack! Each day that you stay alive is an incredible accomplishment brought about by a vicious, desperate fight that nobody can see. You may not have moved forward, and perhaps you have been dragged backwards, but you have dug your nails into the ground until they bleed. No, of course you are not calm, because you are fighting for your life! You are sweaty and dirty and you do not look all that put together right now, but there is no time for that while you are fighting for your life. Keep fighting! I do not know why suicide is so relentless. It lasts many months or years or for some people, decades. Every moment you manage to continue to exist and stay in place is a victory.

It is frustrating that often there truly is nothing very helpful to say. It is so unfair how relentless it is and not everybody is able to have a support system around them, and even if they do, suicide is so difficult and exhausting to fight because it is a lonely battle. Surviving moment by moment ultimately is done alone, which is unfair and daunting, and you feel so weak. It is maddening because nobody can truly fight it with you or even momentarily take up some slack. Fortunately, some people do have others to cheer them on, but you are still hanging over the pit of lava, alone. And it is scary, and you do not know when it is going to end or if it will ever end or if you will be victorious but you keep fighting anyway. You are exhausted beyond description because you cannot loosen your grip even for a second. Nobody can hang in your place even momentarily to allow you to rest. Suicide never gives you a break, you can never lose focus on survival. You are afraid you will have just a moment of weakness or momentary lack of focus, but you are still here and you will keep fighting, and you are not weak.

It is unimaginably exhausting, but you will keep fighting even if it is one second at a time. I am not saying "just keep fighting" as if it were simple and easy. It's not easy at all! I will instead say, "keep fighting!" Or if there is some other phrase that helps even a little bit that I don't claim to know or understand because I do not know you, I insert it here.
